record.paper_title: Control of multi-agent systems: Results, open problems, and applications
record.context_brief: Kantorovich formulation and parsimonious optimal control
record.original_question: For deterministic finite-horizon multi-agent optimal control problems in a Kantorovich formulation, where admissible evolutions are represented by measures on the space of continuous curves and are connected to Lagrangian and Eulerian formulations through the superposition principle, can one characterize sparse or more generally parsimonious admissible or optimal controls and establish necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for such controls within the same framework?

evidence.quote: sparsity, parsimonious controls, and necessary and sufficient conditions

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a time horizon $T>0$, a state space $\mathbb{R}^d$, a control set $U\subset\mathbb{R}^m$ (compact), and a controlled vector field $f:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\times U\to\mathbb{R}^d$ that is continuous, Lipschitz in the state variable uniformly in $(t,u)$, and with linear growth. Let $\Gamma_T:=C([0,T];\mathbb{R}^d)$ denote the space of continuous curves endowed with the uniform topology, and let $e_t:\Gamma_T\to\mathbb{R}^d$ be the evaluation map $e_t(\gamma)=\gamma(t)$.

Given an initial probability measure $\mu_0\in\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ representing the distribution of an infinite population of agents, and a running cost $L:[0,T]\times\mathbb{R}^d\times U\to\mathbb{R}$ together with a terminal cost $\Phi:\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}^d)\to\mathbb{R}$, consider the Kantorovich formulation of the multi-agent optimal control problem:
\[
\inf_{\eta\in\mathcal{A}(\mu_0)} \int_{\Gamma_T}\!\!\int_0^T L(t,\gamma(t),u_\gamma(t))\,dt\,d\eta(\gamma) \;+\; \Phi((e_T)_\#\eta),
\]
where $\mathcal{A}(\mu_0)$ is the set of probability measures $\eta$ on $\Gamma_T$ such that $(e_0)_\#\eta=\mu_0$ and $\eta$-almost every $\gamma$ satisfies $\dot\gamma(t)=f(t,\gamma(t),u_\gamma(t))$ a.e. on $[0,T]$ for some measurable control $u_\gamma:[0,T]\to U$. The superposition principle of Ambrosio relates this Lagrangian-type formulation to the Eulerian continuity equation $\partial_t\mu_t+\mathrm{div}(v_t\mu_t)=0$ with velocity field $v_t$ taking values in $f(t,\cdot,U)$.

Call an admissible $\eta\in\mathcal{A}(\mu_0)$ "parsimonious" if it can be realized using a control strategy that depends measurably on $\gamma$ but is concentrated, in a quantifiable sense, on a low-complexity subset of $\Gamma_T$ (e.g., the set $\{\gamma:u_\gamma\not\equiv 0\}$ has small $\eta$-measure, or the controls $\{u_\gamma\}$ take values in a finite or low-dimensional set $\eta$-a.e.); "sparse" is the special case where this set has measure at most a prescribed threshold.

Problem. Provide a characterization of parsimonious (and in particular sparse) admissible controls in this Kantorovich framework, and derive necessary and sufficient optimality conditions — including a Pontryagin-type maximum principle and/or a Hamilton–Jacobi–Bellman equation on the space of probability measures — that single out parsimonious optimal $\eta^\ast$ minimizing the above cost subject to the constraint $(e_0)_\#\eta=\mu_0$.
artifact.status_search_result: Sparsity and parsimonious control of multi-agent systems have been studied in Lagrangian and mean-field settings (e.g., works by Caponigro, Fornasier, Piccoli, Rossi and collaborators establishing sparse stabilization and sparse Pontryagin principles), but a unified characterization with necessary and sufficient optimality conditions within the Kantorovich/superposition framework remains an active area without a definitive general resolution.

status_evidence.title: Sparse stabilization and control of alignment models
status_evidence.snippet: Develops sparse control strategies for Cucker–Smale-type multi-agent systems, including sparsity-promoting selection principles.
status_evidence.claim: Sparse control for multi-agent systems has been initiated but does not provide a full Kantorovich-level characterization with necessary and sufficient conditions.

status_evidence.title: Mean-field sparse optimal control
status_evidence.snippet: Studies Gamma-limits of sparse optimal control problems toward mean-field formulations using measures on curves.
status_evidence.claim: Mean-field/Kantorovich sparse optimal control has been partially analyzed; full necessary and sufficient optimality conditions remain open in general.
